For example, if the class distribution shows that 99% of the data has the majority class, then any basic classification model like the logistic regression or decision tree will not be able to identify the minor class data points. One way to fight imbalanced data is to generate new samples in the minority classes. SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique in machine learning) works by randomly picking a point from the minority class and computing the k-nearest neighbors for this point. Title: MMSeg: A novel multi-task learning framework for class imbalance and label scarcity in medical image segmentation - ScienceDirect
# MMSeg: A novel multi-task learning framework for class imbalance and label scarcity in medical image segmentation. Semi-supervised medical image segmentation can effectively alleviate the high costs associated with obtaining high-quality labels and issues related to data privacy. In the semi-supervised learning component, we employ a segmentation network with a teacher–student model structure that effectively generates high-confidence pseudo-labels from unlabeled data, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to recognize minority classes. To address this issue, researchers have proposed various semi-supervised methods for medical image segmentation. Currently, fully supervised learning methods for imbalanced medical image segmentation can generally be categorized into reweighting-based approaches or resampling-based approaches. Along these lines, we propose a multi-task medical image segmentation method, the MMSeg. Our multi-task learning framework integrates self-supervised auxiliary tasks with a semi-supervised main task. By combining self-supervised and semi-supervised learning tasks, our model can effectively learn data representations from unlabeled data and make fine adjustments using limited labeled data, ultimately achieving superior segmentation results. Self-supervised tasks extract useful features from this data, helping the model capture the intrinsic structure of medical images and enhancing its ability to generalize to unseen samples. In this section, we explore recent work on our method from three perspectives: (1) semi-supervised imbalance medical image segmentation methods; (2) imbalance medical image analysis; and (3) multi-task learning frameworks. In this section, we provide a detailed overview of the proposed method outlined in Fig. 2, which includes four components: (1) a self-supervised module for helping the model capture the intrinsic structure for imbalance medical images and enhancing its ability to generalize to unseen samples; (2) a semi-supervised module to exploit rich label information from unlabeled images; (3) a progressive learning strategy for prevent potential inefficiencies and fitting difficulties during joint. In this paper, we introduce a novel imbalanced medical image segmentation method based on a multi-task learning framework. This method combines self-supervised learning and semi-supervised learning to enhance the model’s capability to address class imbalance in unlabeled data. * ### KP2L: Knowledge-driven pyramid prototype learning for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. Although few-shot learning has significantly alleviated the dependency of segmentation models on large amounts of labeled data, several challenges remain in applying it to medical image segmentation tasks.
